effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases (the underlying global review of community forest management counts 316 such cases) [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], community forestry in Madagascar had a small but beneficial impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show income gains [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. An Ethiopian area-closure WOCAT compiler rates farm income as improved through selling grass and wood [ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds that they raise overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. A household survey around Malawi's forest reserves by Kimwanga and colleagues finds that taking part in forest co-management through village natural resource management committees, which grants communities legal rights of access and sustainable use of forests, is associated with a 17.48% increase in forestry income and 21.07% in household non-forest income [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_1, ev_household_income_kimwanga26_2], and with a 26.6% higher per capita income among the poorest households in the absence of rainfall shocks [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_6]. After rainfall shocks, participants had 57% higher forestry income and moderately poor households a 31.4% per capita income gain [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_4, ev_household_income_kimwanga26_7]. Participants also owned more durable goods: 3.82% more in Majete and 5.42% more in Vwaza Marsh, a 3.2 higher durable assets index pooled across reserves, and after shocks 2.927 and 2.593 index units more in Majete and Chikangawa [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_9, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_10, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_12, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_13]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Income losses and null findings are substantial. Even the global community-forest review behind the 68% figure records 26% of cases with no change in incomes and 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially harmful effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small beneficial or a neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the supporting evidence is carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. The Malawi co-management gains are uneven across reserves and shocks. After rainfall shocks, participants held fewer durable assets than non-participants in Mua-Livulezi, a 2.846 unit decrease in the asset index, and around Vwaza Marsh, a 1.677 decrease; the authors give no pathway for these losses, which are part of the measured harm on this row [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_11, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14]. Participation did not mitigate the effect of rainfall shocks on non-forestry income, which shocks are likely to erode by 36% among participants too [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_5]. Several of the asset gains and the Vwaza Marsh loss are only weakly significant [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_9, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14], and the study is a cross-sectional comparison of committee members with non-members, not a before-and-after measure. Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh estimate measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. Food-security ratings and findings now sit on the food-insecurity row, and plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations, Costa Rican payments for reforestation plantings and modelled plantation profitability, are reported in their own family rows; neither counts toward this row.

justification.mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases (the underlying global review of community forest management counts 316 such cases) [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], community forestry in Madagascar had a small but beneficial impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show income gains [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. An Ethiopian area-closure WOCAT compiler rates farm income as improved through selling grass and wood [ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds that they raise overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. A household survey around Malawi's forest reserves by Kimwanga and colleagues finds that taking part in forest co-management through village natural resource management committees, which grants communities legal rights of access and sustainable use of forests, is associated with a 17.48% increase in forestry income and 21.07% in household non-forest income [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_1, ev_household_income_kimwanga26_2], and with a 26.6% higher per capita income among the poorest households in the absence of rainfall shocks [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_6]. After rainfall shocks, participants had 57% higher forestry income and moderately poor households a 31.4% per capita income gain [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_4, ev_household_income_kimwanga26_7]. Participants also owned more durable goods: 3.82% more in Majete and 5.42% more in Vwaza Marsh, a 3.2 higher durable assets index pooled across reserves, and after shocks 2.927 and 2.593 index units more in Majete and Chikangawa [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_9, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_10, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_12, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_13]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
justification.conditionality: Income losses and null findings are substantial. Even the global community-forest review behind the 68% figure records 26% of cases with no change in incomes and 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially harmful effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small beneficial or a neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the supporting evidence is carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. The Malawi co-management gains are uneven across reserves and shocks. After rainfall shocks, participants held fewer durable assets than non-participants in Mua-Livulezi, a 2.846 unit decrease in the asset index, and around Vwaza Marsh, a 1.677 decrease; the authors give no pathway for these losses, which are part of the measured harm on this row [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_11, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14]. Participation did not mitigate the effect of rainfall shocks on non-forestry income, which shocks are likely to erode by 36% among participants too [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_5]. Several of the asset gains and the Vwaza Marsh loss are only weakly significant [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_9, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14], and the study is a cross-sectional comparison of committee members with non-members, not a before-and-after measure. Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh estimate measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. Food-security ratings and findings now sit on the food-insecurity row, and plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations, Costa Rican payments for reforestation plantings and modelled plantation profitability, are reported in their own family rows; neither counts toward this row.

effect_mechanism: Planting programmes can raise rural incomes through subsidies, off-farm work and returns on restoration designs, but the evidence gives only the direction and a slight effect. China's Sloping Land Conversion afforestation programme increased off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_iufro20_9], and the programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1].
conditionality: Livelihood losses are documented and are the measured harm on this row: reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection on the land to be reforested without viable alternatives [ev_household_income_le12_1]. The gains come from upper-middle-income China and Brazil, so they transfer to poorer settings only by analogy; the Amazon returns are modelled for agroforestry restoration designs, and the Chinese ratio counts socioeconomic outcomes only and is cited in a systematic review [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. Every unit reaches poverty through income or return proxies, and none quantifies the size of the effect on households. Food-security ratings sit on the food-insecurity row, and plantation results are on the plantation family's poverty row.

effect_mechanism: In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participants, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. In Guanacaste, Costa Rica, payments for environmental services under the reforestation modality made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract, covered a substantial part of the costs of establishing and maintaining the plantation, and brought family employment and legal security over the property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]; similar Latin American programmes reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Modelled plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area feasible for them [ev_economic_return_busch24_1].
conditionality: These are production-plantation results: smallholder plantations, commercial plantations under a payment scheme, and modelled plantations with harvest. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], and the Costa Rica income share comes from a payment scheme rather than from plantation sales alone [ev_household_income_padilla17_1]. The profitability figure is modelled, the effect on poverty is slight, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income and employment. effect_mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed for grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1], the Tanzanian enclosure compiler rates surface runoff as decreased as a result of vegetation cover and downstream siltation as decreased through improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation], and the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], and vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2]. In Tigray, Ethiopia, upstream treatment with deep trenches, percolation pits and afforestation reduced siltation of May Demu dam by up to 60%, a figure the chapter takes from Woldearegay's earlier 2011 report, and in the Abreha Weatsbeha watershed the authors observed significant improvements in reducing soil erosion after afforestation, area closures and water-harvesting works [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, and in Taiwan a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. At community-managed sites the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands and with slowing sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, erosion control structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The Tigray results are bundles of afforestation and area closures with trenches, percolation pits and check-dams, from showcase sites, and the dam figure is an upper bound carried from an earlier report, so neither can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. The erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure, so it sets the direction but not a size [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

justification.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed for grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1], the Tanzanian enclosure compiler rates surface runoff as decreased as a result of vegetation cover and downstream siltation as decreased through improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation], and the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], and vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2]. In Tigray, Ethiopia, upstream treatment with deep trenches, percolation pits and afforestation reduced siltation of May Demu dam by up to 60%, a figure the chapter takes from Woldearegay's earlier 2011 report, and in the Abreha Weatsbeha watershed the authors observed significant improvements in reducing soil erosion after afforestation, area closures and water-harvesting works [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, and in Taiwan a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. At community-managed sites the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands and with slowing sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
justification.conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, erosion control structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The Tigray results are bundles of afforestation and area closures with trenches, percolation pits and check-dams, from showcase sites, and the dam figure is an upper bound carried from an earlier report, so neither can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. The erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure, so it sets the direction but not a size [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

effect_mechanism: In high-income settings the row rests on three units, and none is a measured plot-level soil-loss study. A catchment model of Slovakia's Hornad watershed finds that reforestation results in decreasing surface runoff and flood volume, though it raises interflow, baseflow and evapotranspiration [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]. In Taiwan, reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate set from 1957 data, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A US report cites the conclusion that young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did, so slope protection returns only as the forest matures [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5].
conditionality: The evidence is thin. The Hornad result is a model scenario and covers runoff, a component of erosion risk, not soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]. The Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, cited in an FAO review, so it cannot be credited to tree cover alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The US root-support point is cited second-hand from an earlier study, and it is about how slowly regrowth restores protection, not a measured erosion change [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5]. Missing here: a measured soil-loss or sediment comparison between restored and unrestored land in a high-income setting. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings. Plantation results are kept in their own family rows, out of forest restoration.

effect_mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the evidence is a critical review of China's vegetation restoration programmes, which plant trees, shrubs and grass on hillslopes, a review of erosion in steep tropical terrain, and a meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones. Restored cover protects soil once it is dense enough: once vegetation cover exceeds 60%, the restoration strategy could reduce soil erosion by at least 80%, while below that threshold the erosion-reduction benefit rises sharply with cover [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. In Leyte, Philippines, recovering forest on former slash-and-burn land generated the smallest share of overland flow among the land uses compared, behind fallow pasture, hedgerow systems and mulched cornfields [ev_runoff_reduction_sidle06_1], and on harvested slopes the higher probability of landslides diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2].
conditionality: The class is capped at moderate because few of the units that point the same way say how big the effect is, and the Chinese review itself bounds the gain. In the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, soil conservation measures including vegetation and engineering contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction, so the contribution from vegetation restoration should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]. On the Pearl River the decreased sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures over 20 years [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3], and in 12 small Loess Plateau watersheds the erosion-reduction benefit fell as cover rose, attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. The benefit therefore depends on cover reaching a high threshold and on plantings maturing, and young or sparse restoration may do little. The erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure, so it sets the direction but not a size [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The Philippine and landslide results are cited secondary findings, the landslide one tracking regrowth after timber harvest without separating replanting from natural regeneration [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as less sediment downstream.

effect_mechanism: Review statements that name restoration generically, not a single family, sit here. An FAO regional review of forests and landslides in Asia asserts that tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce risk, and that natural regeneration and tree planting on failed slopes can help control after-effects such as sediment release into rivers [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1]. An FAO forests-and-water synthesis calls forest restoration one of the best ways of restoring productivity and reducing sedimentation in degraded areas of cleared land experiencing accelerated erosion [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1], and lists reducing soil loss and keeping sediment out of streams among the very good reasons for rehabilitating watersheds [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_1]. It cites Taiwan, where reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2]. The effect is off-site for farmers: stabilised slopes and less sediment reaching rivers and reservoirs, at slope and catchment scale rather than on the farm plot.
conditionality: The class is capped at moderate because few units say how large the effect is: the Taiwan reduction and the Tigray dam figure carry sizes, while the FAO statements are assertions without a measured value and the erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The Tigray results are bundles of afforestation and area closures with trenches, percolation pits and check-dams, from showcase sites, and the dam figure is an upper bound carried from an earlier report, so neither can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. The Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control, check dams and gully control, fruit trees and agroforestry, and conservation farming, so it cannot be attributed to forest restoration alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The same synthesis is explicit that achieving substantial flood reduction is not among the reasons to rehabilitate watersheds [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_1]. The Tigray units are the only evidence here from a low-income setting. The primary landslide and watershed studies behind the Asia review are now registered in their own rows (passive regeneration, active planting and protection). Landslide risk is recorded under erosion here for lack of a landslide category.

effect_mechanism: The plantation evidence points both ways, so no direction is stated. Under good tree cover erosion falls: in eucalyptus afforestation in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were substantially greater on a plot with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]. In New Zealand, converting pasture to production forest cuts landslide erosion: in the Waipaoa catchment, calculated landsliding for 1990 and 1995 conditions suggests reforestation over that period produced a 10% decrease in sediment from landslides, equivalent to a 2% decrease in suspended load, and a scenario reforesting the 66 km2 of pasture in the most susceptible areas would cut landslide sediment inputs by 20% [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_1, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_4]; a national model finds new radiata pine forests, once mature, generally reduce mass-movement erosion by an order of magnitude [ev_erosion_hazard_dymond12_1]. Erosion can also worsen under plantations: particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], and an FAO synthesis names dense, planted monocultures with little or no understorey and ground cover as experiencing increased surface erosion rates [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4].

effect_mechanism: This row describes the soil and slope protection that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Forest cover provides the most effective barrier to natural erosion, and loss of forest cover to other land uses always increases human-accelerated erosion unless soil conservation is carried out [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]; in the Ethiopian highlands soil loss under forest averaged 1 tonne per hectare, the lowest of seven categories of land use [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_3]. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: in a US study area the number and acreage of slides increased four and one-half or more times after logging began in 1953, and the scarcity of slides on timbered slopes near logged areas strongly indicates increased susceptibility from logging [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_2]; investigations in steep forested terrain worldwide note up to a 10-fold increase in landslide erosion roughly 3–15 yr after timber harvesting, and rates of mass erosion can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after harvest [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]; mean suspended sediment at managed Sabah catchments was several times higher in the most affected period after logging than before it [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_3]; and in Japan most landslides happened in young forest stands, shrublands and grasslands, the preventive function of the forest increasing with its age class [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_4]. In New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment, deforestation resulted in a 25-fold increase in areal landslide frequency for a 600-mm storm and a 5-fold increase for a 260-mm storm, and on Wharekopae lands, where 35 slides would have been expected had the sampled forest been pasture during storms of 184, 187 and 195 mm, none were observed [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_2, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_3]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil mechanical support [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1]. The WOCAT compiler for community forests in India rates soil loss and downstream siltation as decreased, noting that trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands and helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]; root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. The Waipaoa comparisons set forest against values predicted for pasture, from a forest sample covering a small share of the land studied, and the authors find forest's protection grows with storm size, which sits against the Thailand null below [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_2, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_3]. Nulls stay named: in Thailand landslide density appeared independent of vegetation cover, the storm magnitude overwhelming the stabilising influence of root strength [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_4]; a cited study found lumbering had no part in contributing to slide occurrence and suspected forest maturity of slightly raising slide probability [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_3]; and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The logging, harvest and land-use comparisons are evidence about what existing forest does and what its loss costs, not the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme, which is why they sit in this family and not in the restoration roll-up [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]. The India units are compiler ratings from a sheet that bundles several practices. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as fewer slides and less sediment downslope and downstream.
